title: Worked: build a quadratic, and a complex square root

board_content.text: From a root, and root of a complex number
Real quadratic with one root $2-3i$: the other is $2+3i$.

segments_english.text: Two staple techniques: building a real quadratic from a complex root, and extracting a complex square root.
Suppose a quadratic has real coefficients and one root is two minus three i. By the conjugate-root theorem, the other root must be two plus three i.
Their sum is four, and their product is two minus three i times two plus three i, which is four plus nine, thirteen.
So the quadratic is x squared minus four x plus thirteen equals zero. Fully real, as it must be.
Now a square root: find root of minus fifteen minus eight i. Set it equal to x plus i y and square.
Equating parts gives x squared minus y squared equals minus fifteen, and two x y equals minus eight. The modulus is root of two hundred twenty five plus sixty four, which is seventeen.
So x squared is seventeen minus fifteen, over two, which is one; and y squared is seventeen plus fifteen, over two, which is sixteen. Since two x y is negative, x y is negative.
With x squared one and y squared sixteen and x y negative, the square roots are plus or minus the quantity one minus four i.

segments_hinglish.text: Do staple techniques: complex root se real quadratic banana, aur complex square root nikaalna.
Maano ek quadratic ke real coefficients hain aur ek root two minus three i hai. Conjugate-root theorem se, doosra root two plus three i hona chahiye.
Unka sum hai four, aur product hai two minus three i times two plus three i, jo hai four plus nine, thirteen.
To quadratic hai x squared minus four x plus thirteen equals zero. Poori tarah real, jaisa hona chahiye.
Ab ek square root: root of minus fifteen minus eight i nikaalo. Ise x plus i y ke barabar set karo aur square karo.
Parts equate karne se milta hai x squared minus y squared barabar minus fifteen, aur two x y barabar minus eight. Modulus hai two hundred twenty five plus sixty four ka root, jo hai seventeen.
To x squared hai seventeen minus fifteen, over two, jo hai one; aur y squared hai seventeen plus fifteen, over two, jo hai sixteen. Kyunki two x y negative hai, x y negative hai.
x squared one aur y squared sixteen aur x y negative ke saath, square roots hain plus or minus the quantity one minus four i.
